records.source: Τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἐκκλησίας γράψον· Τάδε λέγει ὁ κρατῶν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἀστέρας ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ, ὁ περιπατῶν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ἑπτὰ λυχνιῶν τῶν χρυσῶν·
records.gloss: To the angel of the in Ephesus church write: These things says the [one] holding the seven stars in the right [hand] of him, the [one] walking in [the] middle of the seven lampstands the golden:
pieces: To the angel of the church in Ephesus, write: "This is the message of the one who grips the seven stars in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand, who walks about among the seven lampstands of gold:

L.1: To the angel of the church in Ephesus write: "These things says the one who holds the seven stars in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right [hand], the one who walks in [the] middle of the seven golden lampstands:

R.1: Write this letter to the angel of the church in Ephesus: "This message is from the one who holds the seven stars tightly in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand and walks among the seven gold lampstands.

decisions.choice: these things says: the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word
decisions.reason: Τάδε λέγει recalls the prophets' "Thus says the LORD", which the Greek Old Testament renders with the same words. Each of the seven letters opens with it, and what follows is the speaker's own description from the vision in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: holds firmly, and walks among: his grip on the churches and his presence with them
decisions.reason: In 1:16 he "has" the stars; here κρατῶν means to grasp or hold firmly. And he does not only stand among the lampstands (1:13) but περιπατῶν, walks among them: he is present with the churches and watches over them.

decisions.choice: Ephesus: the leading city of the province of Asia
decisions.reason: Ephesus was a port and the largest city of the province, with the great temple of Artemis (Acts 19). Paul worked there for more than two years (Acts 19:10), and it is the first city a messenger from Patmos would reach.

decisions.choice: angel (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 1:20 says the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and every level keeps "angel" here as there. The note on 1:20 gives the other view.

records.heading: To the church in Ephesus

records.source: Οἶδα τὰ ἔργα σου, καὶ τὸν κόπον καὶ τὴν ὑπομονήν σου, καὶ ὅτι οὐ δύνῃ βαστάσαι κακούς, καὶ ἐπείρασας τοὺς λέγοντας ἑαυτοὺς ἀποστόλους, καὶ οὐκ εἰσίν, καὶ εὗρες αὐτοὺς ψευδεῖς·
records.gloss: I know the works of you and the labor and the endurance of you, and that not you are able to bear bad [ones], and you tested those calling themselves apostles and not they are, and you found them false;
pieces: I know your works, how hard you have labored and how you have endured. I know that you cannot put up with people who do evil. Those who call themselves apostles, though they are not, you put to the test and found to be false.

L.2: I know your works, and your labor and endurance, and that you cannot bear evil [people], and you tested those who call themselves apostles and are not, and you found them false.

R.2: I know everything you do. I know how hard you work and how you keep going. I know that you will not put up with evil people. Some people said they were apostles, but they were not. You tested them and found out that they were lying.

decisions.choice: your works: what you do, your whole way of life
decisions.reason: ἔργα is a broad word for deeds and conduct. Each letter begins "I know" (2:2, 9, 13, 19; 3:1, 8, 15): the speaker who walks among the churches knows them as they are.

decisions.choice: false apostles: travelling teachers who claimed an apostle's authority
decisions.reason: Apostle means one who is sent. Besides the Twelve and Paul, others were called apostles (Acts 14:14), and travelling teachers who claimed the title came to churches (2 Corinthians 11:13; 1 John 4:1). Paul had warned the Ephesian elders that false teachers would come (Acts 20:29-30). The church at Ephesus tested such people and found them false.

decisions.choice: cannot bear: cannot tolerate evil people among them
decisions.reason: βαστάσαι means to carry or bear. Here, with evil people as its object, it means to put up with them. The same verb comes back in 2:3 in its other sense: they have borne hardship for Christ's name.

decisions.choice: Those who call themselves apostles ... you put to the test (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the false apostles first so that the clause "though they are not" stays next to their claim.

records.source: καὶ ὑπομονὴν ἔχεις, καὶ ἐβάστασας διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου, καὶ οὐ κεκοπίακες.
records.gloss: and endurance you have, and you bore on account of the name of me, and not you have grown weary.
pieces: You keep going. For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name's sake you have carried heavy loads, and you have not grown tired.

L.3: And you have endurance, and you have borne [up] because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and you have not grown weary.

R.3: You keep going and do not give up. You have suffered hard things because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you have not become tired of it.

decisions.choice: plays on words: they bear hardship though they cannot bear evil; they labor and have not grown weary
decisions.reason: ἐβάστασας repeats the verb of 2:2, "bear": they cannot bear evil people, yet they have borne hardship. κεκοπίακες is from the same root as "labor" in 2:2: they have labored, and the labor has not worn them out.

decisions.choice: because of my name: because they belong to Jesus and bear his name
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. To suffer for his name is to suffer because one is known as his (Acts 5:41; Matthew 10:22).

decisions.choice: because you belong to me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "my name" means here (m2).

records.source: ἀλλὰ ἔχω κατὰ σοῦ ὅτι τὴν ἀγάπην σου τὴν πρώτην ἀφῆκες.
records.gloss: But I have against you that the love of you the first you left.
pieces: But here is my complaint against you: the love you had in the beginning, you have let go.

L.4: But I have [this] against you, that you have left your first love.

R.4: But there is one thing I have against you. You have stopped loving the way you loved at the beginning.

decisions.choice: the first love: the love they had at first, and the love that should come first
decisions.reason: πρώτην means first in time, and here it points back to the church's early days, as "the first works" do in 2:5. It may also carry the sense of what comes first in importance.

decisions.choice: love for Christ and love for one another, which the text does not separate
decisions.reason: The text does not say whom they have stopped loving. In John's writings love for God and love for fellow believers go together (1 John 4:20-21). A church that tests and rejects false teachers can grow hard toward its own members, and that may be the danger here. The object is left unstated.

decisions.choice: left behind: abandoned, not merely cooled
decisions.reason: ἀφῆκες means to let go or leave. The love is not said to have weakened but to have been left behind, which is why 2:5 calls for repentance.

records.source: μνημόνευε οὖν πόθεν πέπτωκας, καὶ μετανόησον καὶ τὰ πρῶτα ἔργα ποίησον· εἰ δὲ μή, ἔρχομαί σοι, καὶ κινήσω τὴν λυχνίαν σου ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτῆς, ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσῃς.
records.gloss: Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and repent and the first works do; but if not, I am coming to you and I will move the lampstand of you out of the place of it, if not you repent.
pieces: So call to mind the height you have fallen from. Repent, and act as you did at the start. Otherwise I am coming to you, and I will move your lampstand from where it stands, unless you repent.

L.5: Remember, then, from where you have fallen, and repent and do the first works. But if not, I am coming to you, and I will move your lampstand out of its place, unless you repent.

R.5: So remember what you were like before you fell. Turn away from your sins and do the things you did at first. If you do not, I will come to you and take your lampstand away from its place. That will happen unless you change.

decisions.choice: repent: turn around in mind and life
decisions.reason: μετανόησον means to change one's mind, and in the Bible it means turning from sin to God in thought and action. The command is in a form that calls for a decisive turn. Repentance is a call in five of the seven letters (2:5, 16, 21-22; 3:3, 19).

decisions.choice: removing the lampstand: the church would cease to be a church that bears his light
alternatives: the city's church would be moved elsewhere
decisions.reason: The lampstands are the churches (1:20). To move a lampstand from its place is to end that church's existence as a church, or its place as a light among the churches. The threat is about the church as a body, not about each believer's salvation.

decisions.choice: I am coming to you: a coming in judgment on this church
decisions.reason: "I am coming" is present, with a future sense. Here it is conditional ("if not") and aimed at one church, so it is most likely a visit of judgment within history, not the final coming, which does not depend on whether Ephesus repents. Revelation also speaks of the final coming in the same words (22:7, 20).

decisions.choice: repent (L, B); turn away from your sins, change (R)
decisions.reason: "Repent" is the familiar word and is kept at Literal and Balanced. Readable says what it means in plain words.

records.source: ἀλλὰ τοῦτο ἔχεις ὅτι μισεῖς τὰ ἔργα τῶν Νικολαϊτῶν, ἃ κἀγὼ μισῶ.
records.gloss: But this you have, that you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
pieces: Yet there is this to your credit: you hate the things the Nicolaitans do, and so do I.

L.6: But you have this: that you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.

R.6: But you do one thing that is good. You hate what the Nicolaitans do. I hate it too.

decisions.choice: the Nicolaitans: a group known only from Revelation
decisions.reason: The New Testament names the Nicolaitans only here and in 2:15, where their teaching is set beside Balaam's: eating food sacrificed to idols and sexual immorality (2:14). Some early Christian writers connected them with Nicolaus of Antioch (Acts 6:5), but that link cannot be confirmed. The letter does not describe them further.

decisions.choice: it is what they do that is hated
decisions.reason: The object of the hatred is ἔργα, the works, not the people. The church shares the hatred of the one who speaks.

records.source: ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.
records.gloss: The [one] having an ear let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
pieces: Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.

L.7: The one who has an ear, let {{gender:that person|him}} hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

R.7: Everyone who can hear should listen carefully to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.

decisions.choice: an echo of Jesus's saying in the Gospels: whoever has ears, let them hear
decisions.reason: Jesus closes parables with these words in the Gospels (Matthew 11:15; 13:9, 43; Mark 4:9). They call for more than hearing sounds: the hearer is to take the message in and act on it. Each of the seven letters ends with the call (2:7, 11, 17, 29; 3:6, 13, 22), and 13:9 repeats it.

decisions.choice: the Spirit speaks the risen Jesus's words, and each letter is for every church
decisions.reason: The letter is spoken by the risen Jesus (2:1), yet the call says it is what the Spirit says. The words of Christ come to the churches through the Spirit, as John was "in the Spirit" when he heard them (1:10). "Churches" is plural: what is written to one church is meant for all seven, and for every church that hears it.

decisions.choice: The one who has an ear, let that person hear (L); Whoever has ears should listen (B, R)
alternatives: He who has an ear, let him hear
decisions.reason: The Greek uses a masculine form for anyone at all. Literal keeps the form with a gender setting; Balanced and Readable use "whoever" and "everyone", which need no setting. English says "ears" where the Greek has the singular.

records.source: τῷ νικῶντι δώσω αὐτῷ φαγεῖν ἐκ τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: To the [one] overcoming I will give to him to eat from the tree of the life, which is in the paradise of the God.
pieces: I will let everyone who overcomes eat from the tree of life that grows in God's paradise."

L.7: To the one who overcomes, to {{gender:that person|him}} I will give [the right] to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God."

R.7: I will let everyone who wins the victory eat from the tree of life, which grows in God's garden, paradise."

decisions.choice: the one who overcomes: who wins the victory by staying faithful
decisions.reason: νικῶντι means to win or conquer. Each letter ends with a promise to the one who overcomes (2:7, 11, 17, 26; 3:5, 12, 21). In Revelation the victory is won as the Lamb won it, by faithful witness even to death (3:21; 5:5-6; 12:11), not by force.

decisions.choice: the tree of life in the garden of Eden, restored
decisions.reason: The tree of life grew in the garden of Eden (Genesis 2:9), and after their disobedience the man and the woman were kept from it (Genesis 3:22-24). παραδείσῳ was a word for a garden or park, and the Greek Old Testament uses it for Eden. The promise is that what was lost will be given back; Revelation 22:2, 14 shows the tree again in the new Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: to the one who overcomes, to that person (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek names the person and then repeats him with αὐτῷ, "to him". English does not need both, so only Literal shows the repetition, here and in 2:17 and 2:26.

decisions.choice: overcomes (L, B); wins the victory (R)
decisions.reason: "Overcome" says winning through against opposition, and suits a victory won by endurance (m1). Readable uses plain words.

records.source: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Σμύρνῃ ἐκκλησίας γράψον· Τάδε λέγει ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος, ὃς ἐγένετο νεκρὸς καὶ ἔζησεν·
records.gloss: And to the angel of the in Smyrna church write: These things says the first and the last, who became dead and came to life:
pieces: To the angel of the church in Smyrna, write: "This is the message of the first and the last, the one who was dead and came to life:

L.8: And to the angel of the church in Smyrna write: "These things says the first and the last, who became dead and came to life:

R.8: Write this letter to the angel of the church in Smyrna: "This message is from the first and the last, the one who died and came back to life.

decisions.choice: these things says: the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word
decisions.reason: Τάδε λέγει recalls the prophets' "Thus says the LORD", which the Greek Old Testament renders with the same words. Each of the seven letters opens with it, and what follows is the speaker's own description from the vision in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: the titles from 1:17-18
decisions.reason: The speaker is described with his own words from 1:17-18. To a church facing prison and death (2:10), he speaks as the one who died and lives.

decisions.choice: Smyrna: a wealthy port north of Ephesus, long loyal to Rome
decisions.reason: Smyrna (modern Izmir) was a large and prosperous city that had built a temple to the goddess Roma and later one to the emperor Tiberius. Its church was poor and under pressure (2:9).

decisions.choice: angel (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 1:20 says the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and every level keeps "angel" here as there. The note on 1:20 gives the other view.

records.heading: To the church in Smyrna

records.source: Οἶδά σου τὴν θλῖψιν καὶ τὴν πτωχείαν, ἀλλὰ πλούσιος εἶ, καὶ τὴν βλασφημίαν ἐκ τῶν λεγόντων Ἰουδαίους εἶναι ἑαυτούς, καὶ οὐκ εἰσίν, ἀλλὰ συναγωγὴ τοῦ Σατανᾶ.
records.gloss: I know of you the affliction and the poverty—but rich you are—and the slander from those saying Jews to be themselves, and not they are, but a synagogue of the Satan.
pieces: I know your affliction and your poverty—though in fact you are rich—and the abuse you receive from those who claim to be Jews but are not. They are Satan's synagogue.

L.9: I know your affliction and poverty—but you are rich—and the slander of those who say they are Jews and are not, but [are] a synagogue of Satan.

R.9: I know about your troubles and that you are poor. But really you are rich! I know that some people say evil things about you. They say they are Jews, but they are not. Their meeting place belongs to Satan.

decisions.choice: rich: rich before God, though poor in money
decisions.reason: The church is poor in the world's terms, perhaps because believers lost work or property, but rich in what counts with God (compare James 2:5). The letter to Laodicea says the reverse (3:17).

decisions.choice: slander: abuse spoken against the believers
decisions.reason: βλασφημίαν can mean speech against God or harmful speech against people. Here it comes from people and falls on the church, so it is slander, perhaps including accusations to the authorities.

decisions.choice: a local group who opposed the church, not the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: John was himself a Jew, and for him the name "Jew" was a name of honor (compare Romans 2:28-29). He says that these particular people in Smyrna, who slander the believers, do not live up to the name, and that in opposing Christ's people they are doing the work of Satan, whose name means "accuser". The words are about one group in one city at one time. They give no ground for hostility toward Jewish people.

decisions.choice: synagogue: a gathering or assembly
decisions.reason: συναγωγὴ means a gathering, and was the usual word for a Jewish congregation and its meeting place. "Synagogue of Satan" turns the word against those who used it of themselves; 3:9 uses the phrase again.

decisions.choice: Their meeting place belongs to Satan (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "synagogue" as a place where people meet; the theology decision says what the phrase does and does not mean.

records.source: μηδὲν φοβοῦ ἃ μέλλεις πάσχειν.
records.gloss: Nothing fear what things you are about to suffer.
pieces: Have no fear of anything you are going to suffer.

L.10: Do not fear [any of] the things you are about to suffer.

R.10: Do not be afraid of the suffering that is coming to you.

decisions.choice: do not fear anything: a command that also says suffering is coming
decisions.reason: μηδὲν φοβοῦ is emphatic: fear nothing of what lies ahead. The command does not promise that suffering will be avoided; it says that it will come and that they need not fear it.

records.source: ἰδοὺ μέλλει βάλλειν ὁ διάβολος ἐξ ὑμῶν εἰς φυλακὴν ἵνα πειρασθῆτε, καὶ ἕξετε θλῖψιν ἡμερῶν δέκα.
records.gloss: Behold, is about to throw the devil [some] of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction of days ten.
pieces: Look: some of you the devil is about to throw into prison, so that you will be tested, and you will face affliction for ten days.

L.10: Look, the devil is about to throw [some] of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction ten days.

R.10: Listen! The devil will soon have some of you thrown into prison. This will test you. For ten days you will suffer.

decisions.choice: prison: where people were held before trial or execution
decisions.reason: Roman prisons were mostly a place to hold the accused until they were tried, punished or put to death, not a sentence in themselves. So imprisonment could lead to death, and 2:10 goes on, "be faithful to death".

decisions.choice: tested: put to a trial that shows whether they stand
decisions.reason: πειρασθῆτε can mean to test or to tempt. The devil means harm, but the trial proves their faithfulness. Both senses lie close together, as in Job 1-2.

decisions.choice: ten days: a short time, and a limited one
decisions.reason: Ten days may be a literal span, but it most likely means a short, fixed period that God has set, as in Daniel 1:12-15, where Daniel and his friends are tested for ten days. The suffering is real, and it has an end.

decisions.choice: Look (L, B); Listen (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide does not use "behold". Readable uses "Listen", which calls a young reader to attention in a spoken message.

records.source: γίνου πιστὸς ἄχρι θανάτου, καὶ δώσω σοι τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς.
records.gloss: Be faithful until death, and I will give to you the crown of the life.
pieces: Stay faithful even to death, and I will give you the crown of life.

L.10: Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.

R.10: Stay faithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, even if it means you must die. Then I will give you the winner's crown, which is life that lasts forever.

decisions.choice: until death: to the point of dying, if it comes to that
alternatives: all your life, until you die
decisions.reason: ἄχρι θανάτου can mean up to the end of one's life, but after the warning of prison it most likely means faithful even when faithfulness costs one's life (compare 12:11).

decisions.choice: the crown: the wreath given to a winner
decisions.reason: στέφανον was the wreath of leaves given to the winner of a contest, or to someone honored by a city. It was not a king's crown, for which there is another word (19:12). The promise is the victor's reward.

decisions.choice: the crown that is life
decisions.reason: "Crown of life" most likely means the crown which is life itself: eternal life is the prize (as in James 1:12).

decisions.choice: to me; the winner's crown, which is life that lasts forever (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom they are faithful and explains the picture (m2, m3).

records.source: ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.
records.gloss: The [one] having an ear let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
pieces: Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.

L.11: The one who has an ear, let {{gender:that person|him}} hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

R.11: Everyone who can hear should listen carefully to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.

decisions.choice: the call that closes every letter
decisions.reason: The same call ends each of the seven letters; see the notes on 2:7. What the risen Jesus says to one church, the Spirit says to all of them.

records.source: ὁ νικῶν οὐ μὴ ἀδικηθῇ ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου τοῦ δευτέρου.
records.gloss: The [one] overcoming by no means will be harmed by the death the second.
pieces: The second death will never harm anyone who overcomes."

L.11: The one who overcomes will certainly not be harmed by the second death."

R.11: Everyone who wins the victory will be safe from the second death. It will never hurt them."

decisions.choice: the second death: final judgment, after the death of the body
decisions.reason: Revelation explains the phrase itself: the second death is the lake of fire (20:14; 21:8), and it has no power over those who share in the first resurrection (20:6). Believers in Smyrna may die the first death (2:10), but not the second.

decisions.choice: a strong denial: certainly not
decisions.reason: οὐ μὴ together make the strongest Greek denial.

records.source: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Περγάμῳ ἐκκλησίας γράψον· Τάδε λέγει ὁ ἔχων τὴν ῥομφαίαν τὴν δίστομον τὴν ὀξεῖαν·
records.gloss: And to the angel of the in Pergamum church write: These things says the [one] having the sword the two-edged the sharp:
pieces: To the angel of the church in Pergamum, write: "This is the message of the one who has the sharp sword with two edges:

L.12: And to the angel of the church in Pergamum write: "These things says the one who has the sharp two-edged sword:

R.12: Write this letter to the angel of the church in Pergamum: "This message is from the one who has the sharp sword with two edges.

decisions.choice: these things says: the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word
decisions.reason: Τάδε λέγει recalls the prophets' "Thus says the LORD", which the Greek Old Testament renders with the same words. Each of the seven letters opens with it, and what follows is the speaker's own description from the vision in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: the sword from his mouth (1:16)
decisions.reason: This is the sword that comes from his mouth in 1:16, and 2:16 says he will fight with it. It stands for the power of his word to judge.

decisions.choice: Pergamum: a royal city and a center of worship of the emperor
decisions.reason: Pergamum, north of Smyrna, had been a royal capital and was a seat of Roman government in the province. In 29 BC it built the first temple in Asia to Augustus and Rome. It also had a great altar to Zeus and a famous shrine of the healing god Asclepius.

decisions.choice: angel (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 1:20 says the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and every level keeps "angel" here as there. The note on 1:20 gives the other view.

records.heading: To the church in Pergamum

records.source: Οἶδα ποῦ κατοικεῖς, ὅπου ὁ θρόνος τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ κρατεῖς τὸ ὄνομά μου, καὶ οὐκ ἠρνήσω τὴν πίστιν μου καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἀντιπᾶς, ὁ μάρτυς μου, ὁ πιστός μου, ὃς ἀπεκτάνθη παρ’ ὑμῖν, ὅπου ὁ Σατανᾶς κατοικεῖ.
records.gloss: I know where you dwell, where the throne of the Satan [is], and you hold fast the name of me, and not you denied the faith of me even in the days of Antipas, the witness of me, the faithful [one] of me, who was killed among you, where the Satan dwells.
pieces: I know where you make your home: the place of Satan's throne. Still you keep a firm grip on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. Even in the days of Antipas, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witness and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful one, who was killed among you where Satan lives, you did not disown your faith in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.13: I know where you live, where the throne of Satan [is]; and you hold fast {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and you did not deny {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faith even in the days of Antipas, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witness, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan lives.

R.13: I know where you live. It is the city where Satan has his throne. But you hold on tightly to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You did not give up your faith in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, even when Antipas was killed in your city. He was {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witness and was faithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Your city is where Satan lives.

decisions.choice: the throne of Satan: Pergamum as a center of the powers opposed to Christ
alternatives: the shrine of Asclepius, whose sign was a serpent
decisions.reason: The text does not say what made Pergamum the place of Satan's throne, and several features of the city have been suggested (see the culture note on 2:12). Since Antipas was killed there, the worship of the emperor and the Roman power to put people to death may be in view.

decisions.choice: my faith: faith in me
alternatives: the faith that is mine, the faith I taught
decisions.reason: "My faith" most likely means their faith in Jesus, which they did not deny even when it could cost their lives. It may also mean faithfulness to him.

decisions.choice: Antipas, my witness: one who bore witness to Jesus and was killed for it
decisions.reason: Antipas is known only from this verse. μάρτυς means a witness, and Jesus is "the faithful witness" (1:5); Antipas shares the title. The word later came to mean a martyr because so many witnesses died. The Greek leaves his name in the form of a subject where another form is expected, as John does with a title in 1:4.

decisions.choice: hold on tightly to me (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:3, "my name" means Jesus himself, and Readable says so.

records.source: ἀλλὰ ἔχω κατὰ σοῦ ὀλίγα, ὅτι ἔχεις ἐκεῖ κρατοῦντας τὴν διδαχὴν Βαλαάμ, ὃς ἐδίδασκεν τῷ Βαλὰκ βαλεῖν σκάνδαλον ἐνώπιον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, φαγεῖν εἰδωλόθυτα καὶ πορνεῦσαι·
records.gloss: But I have against you a few things, that you have there [those] holding the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to throw a stumbling block before the sons of Israel, to eat idol-sacrifices and to commit sexual immorality;
pieces: But I have a few complaints against you. You have people there who hold to what Balaam taught. He showed Balak how to set a trap for the Israelites, so that they would eat food offered to idols and commit sexual immorality.

L.14: But I have a few things against you: you have there [some] who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to put a stumbling block before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols and to commit sexual immorality.

R.14: But I have a few things against you. Some people in your church follow the teaching of Balaam. Long ago Balaam taught King Balak how to make the Israelites sin. Balak got them to eat food that had been offered to idols and to commit sexual sins.

decisions.choice: Balaam and Balak: Numbers 22-25 and 31:16
decisions.reason: Balak king of Moab hired the prophet Balaam to curse Israel (Numbers 22-24). Balaam could only bless, but Numbers 31:16 says it was on his advice that the Israelites were drawn into the worship of Baal of Peor, with its sacrificial meals and sexual sin (Numbers 25:1-3). Balaam became a byword for a teacher who leads God's people astray for gain (2 Peter 2:15; Jude 11).

decisions.choice: food sacrificed to idols: meat from pagan sacrifices, eaten at temple meals or bought in the market
decisions.reason: Much of the meat in a Greek city came from sacrifices, and feasts of trade associations and families were often held in temples. Paul discusses the question in 1 Corinthians 8-10, and the Jerusalem council asked believers to keep away from such food (Acts 15:29).

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: real sexual sin, and perhaps also unfaithfulness to God
decisions.reason: πορνεῦσαι means sexual immorality. The prophets also used the picture of prostitution for Israel's worship of other gods (Hosea 4:12-13), and Revelation uses it of Babylon (17:2). At Peor both were real: sexual sin and idol worship went together (Numbers 25:1-2). The text may mean both here.

decisions.choice: a stumbling block: a trap that makes someone fall into sin
decisions.reason: σκάνδαλον was the trigger of a trap, and came to mean anything that causes a fall.

decisions.choice: children of Israel (L); the Israelites (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Sons of Israel" means the people of Israel, men and women. Literal keeps the form under the gender setting; Balanced and Readable say "Israelites".

records.source: οὕτως ἔχεις καὶ σὺ κρατοῦντας τὴν διδαχὴν Νικολαϊτῶν ὁμοίως.
records.gloss: So you have also you [those] holding the teaching of [the] Nicolaitans likewise.
pieces: You also have, in the same way, people who cling to the Nicolaitans' teaching.

L.15: So you also have [some] who hold the teaching of [the] Nicolaitans in the same way.

R.15: In the same way, some of your people follow the teaching of the Nicolaitans.

decisions.choice: in the same way: the Nicolaitans teach what Balaam taught
decisions.reason: οὕτως and ὁμοίως, "so" and "likewise", most likely compare the Nicolaitans with Balaam: their teaching leads to the same sins. They may be the same people under two names. The letter could also mean a second group as well as the first.

records.source: μετανόησον οὖν· εἰ δὲ μή, ἔρχομαί σοι ταχύ, καὶ πολεμήσω μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ῥομφαίᾳ τοῦ στόματός μου.
records.gloss: Repent therefore; but if not, I am coming to you quickly, and I will make war against them with the sword of the mouth of me.
pieces: Repent, then. Otherwise I am coming to you soon, and I will wage war on them with the sword that comes from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth.

L.16: Repent, then. But if not, I am coming to you quickly, and I will make war against them with the sword of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth.

R.16: So turn away from your sins! If you do not, I will come to you soon. I will fight against those people with the sword that comes out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth.

decisions.choice: coming to you, fighting against them
decisions.reason: The whole church is told to repent, since it tolerates the teachers; the war is against "them", those who hold the teaching. The church's coming is a warning; the judgment falls on the false teachers.

decisions.choice: the sword and Balaam
decisions.reason: An angel stood against Balaam with a drawn sword (Numbers 22:23, 31), and Balaam was killed with the sword (Numbers 31:8). Here the sword is the one from Christ's mouth (1:16; 2:12): his word.

decisions.choice: soon
decisions.reason: ταχύ can mean soon or quickly; see the note on 1:1.

records.source: ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.
records.gloss: The [one] having an ear let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
pieces: Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.

L.17: The one who has an ear, let {{gender:that person|him}} hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

R.17: Everyone who can hear should listen carefully to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.

decisions.choice: the call that closes every letter
decisions.reason: The same call ends each of the seven letters; see the notes on 2:7. What the risen Jesus says to one church, the Spirit says to all of them.

records.source: τῷ νικῶντι δώσω αὐτῷ τοῦ μάννα τοῦ κεκρυμμένου, καὶ δώσω αὐτῷ ψῆφον λευκήν, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ψῆφον ὄνομα καινὸν γεγραμμένον ὃ οὐδεὶς οἶδεν εἰ μὴ ὁ λαμβάνων.
records.gloss: To the [one] overcoming I will give to him of the manna the hidden, and I will give to him a stone white, and on the stone a name new having been written, which no one knows except the [one] receiving.
pieces: To everyone who overcomes I will give a share of the hidden manna. I will give each one a white stone too, and written on the stone is a new name that only the one who receives it knows."

L.17: To the one who overcomes, to {{gender:that person|him}} I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give {{gender:that person|him}} a white stone, and on the stone a new name written, which no one knows except the one who receives [it]."

R.17: I will give everyone who wins the victory some of the hidden manna, the bread from heaven. I will also give each of them a white stone with a new name written on it. Only the person who receives the stone will know that name."

decisions.choice: the hidden manna: the bread God gave in the wilderness, kept for the age to come
decisions.reason: God fed Israel with manna in the wilderness (Exodus 16), and a jar of it was kept before the Lord in the ark (Exodus 16:32-34; Hebrews 9:4). Jewish writings from about John's time expected the manna to come down again in the age of the Messiah (2 Baruch 29:8). Jesus calls himself the bread from heaven (John 6:31-35). Those who refuse food sacrificed to idols (2:14) are promised God's own food.

decisions.choice: a white stone: its meaning is uncertain
alternatives: a white voting stone that meant acquittal
a token of admission to a feast
a stone with a name carried as a sign of favor
decisions.reason: ψῆφον was a small, smooth stone. Such stones were used in voting, a white one for acquittal, and as tickets to banquets and public events. White is the color of victory and purity in Revelation (3:4-5). The text does not say which use is meant; a token of welcome to the feast fits the manna best, but none is certain.

decisions.choice: a new name: most likely the new name given to the believer
alternatives: the name of Christ, which only those who belong to him know
decisions.reason: Isaiah 62:2 and 65:15 promise God's people a new name. In 3:12 Christ writes his own new name on the one who overcomes, and in 19:12 he has a name no one knows but himself. Here the name is known only to the one who receives the stone, which points to a name given to the believer, but the two cannot be wholly separated.

decisions.choice: the bread from heaven (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what manna was, using the Bible's own description (Psalm 78:24; John 6:31).

records.source: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Θυατείροις ἐκκλησίας γράψον· Τάδε λέγει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, ὁ ἔχων τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ ὡς φλόγα πυρός, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὅμοιοι χαλκολιβάνῳ·
records.gloss: And to the angel of the in Thyatira church write: These things says the Son of the God, the [one] having the eyes of him like flame of fire, and the feet of him like to fine bronze:
pieces: To the angel of the church in Thyatira, write: "This is the message of the Son of God, whose eyes are like a flame of fire and whose feet are like fine bronze:

L.18: And to the angel of the church in Thyatira write: "These things says the Son of God, who has {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes like a flame of fire, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet [are] like fine bronze:

R.18: Write this letter to the angel of the church in Thyatira: "This message is from the Son of God. His eyes are like flames of fire, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet are like shining bronze.

decisions.choice: these things says: the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word
decisions.reason: Τάδε λέγει recalls the prophets' "Thus says the LORD", which the Greek Old Testament renders with the same words. Each of the seven letters opens with it, and what follows is the speaker's own description from the vision in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: the Son of God: the king of Psalm 2
decisions.reason: This is the only place Revelation uses the title. The letter ends by quoting Psalm 2:9 (2:27), and in Psalm 2:7 God says to his king, "You are my Son". The title fits a letter about authority over the nations.

decisions.choice: the eyes and feet from 1:14-15
decisions.reason: The description comes from 1:14-15. Eyes like fire see everything; 2:23 says he searches minds and hearts. On "fine bronze" see the note on 1:15.

decisions.choice: Thyatira: a city of trade guilds
decisions.reason: Thyatira was an inland city known for its many trade associations, including dyers (Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth, came from there, Acts 16:14). Belonging to a guild could mean sharing its feasts in honor of its gods, which may lie behind the teaching in 2:20.

decisions.choice: angel (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 1:20 says the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and every level keeps "angel" here as there. The note on 1:20 gives the other view.

records.heading: To the church in Thyatira

records.source: Οἶδά σου τὰ ἔργα, καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην καὶ τὴν πίστιν καὶ τὴν διακονίαν καὶ τὴν ὑπομονήν σου, καὶ τὰ ἔργα σου τὰ ἔσχατα πλείονα τῶν πρώτων.
records.gloss: I know of you the works and the love and the faith and the service and the endurance of you, and the works of you the last more than the first.
pieces: I know your works—the love, the faith, the service, the endurance that are yours—and that your recent works outnumber your first ones.

L.19: I know your works, and your love and faith and service and endurance, and [that] your last works [are] more than the first.

R.19: I know everything you do. I know your love and your faith. I know how you serve and how you keep going. You are doing even more now than you did at first.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in Christ, which shows itself in faithfulness
decisions.reason: πίστιν can mean faith or faithfulness. Here it stands in a list of what the church does and is, beside love, service and endurance, and the sense of steady faithfulness is close.

decisions.choice: two pairs: love shown in service, faith shown in endurance
decisions.reason: The four nouns may be read as two pairs, love with service and faith with endurance, but the list does not require it.

decisions.choice: growth: the opposite of Ephesus
decisions.reason: Ephesus was told to go back to its first works (2:5). Thyatira's later works are more than its first: the church is growing in what it does.

records.source: ἀλλὰ ἔχω κατὰ σοῦ ὅτι ἀφεῖς τὴν γυναῖκα Ἰεζάβελ, ἡ λέγουσα ἑαυτὴν προφῆτιν, καὶ διδάσκει καὶ πλανᾷ τοὺς ἐμοὺς δούλους πορνεῦσαι καὶ φαγεῖν εἰδωλόθυτα.
records.gloss: But I have against you that you tolerate the woman Jezebel, the [one] calling herself a prophetess, and she teaches and deceives the my slaves to commit sexual immorality and to eat idol-sacrifices.
pieces: But I hold this against you: you put up with the woman Jezebel, the self-styled prophet. She teaches {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants and deceives them into sexual immorality and into eating food offered to idols.

L.20: But I have [this] against you: that you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, and she teaches and leads astray {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slaves to commit sexual immorality and to eat things sacrificed to idols.

R.20: But I have something against you. You allow that woman Jezebel to do as she likes. She says she is a prophet, but she teaches {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants wrong things. She tricks them into sexual sins and into eating food that was offered to idols.

decisions.choice: Jezebel: a name taken from the queen who led Israel into Baal worship
decisions.reason: Jezebel, wife of King Ahab, brought the worship of Baal into Israel and was remembered for her "harlotries and sorceries" (1 Kings 16:31; 21:25; 2 Kings 9:22). The woman in Thyatira was a real person in the church, but the name is most likely given to her because she led God's people into the same sins. It is unlikely to be her own name.

decisions.choice: the woman Jezebel
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "the woman". Some manuscripts add "your" after it, which would make her the wife of the "angel", read as the church's leader. The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: she calls herself a prophet; Christ does not
decisions.reason: She claims to speak for God, and the church lets her teach. The words "calling herself" echo the false apostles of 2:2 and the false Jews of 2:9: a claim that does not match the truth.

decisions.choice: the same two sins as at Pergamum
decisions.reason: Sexual immorality and food sacrificed to idols are the sins of Balaam's teaching (2:14); see the notes there.

decisions.choice: prophetess (L); prophet (B, R)
decisions.reason: προφῆτιν is the feminine form of the word for prophet. Literal shows the form; modern English uses "prophet" for a woman as well as a man.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it (1:1); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: καὶ ἔδωκα αὐτῇ χρόνον ἵνα μετανοήσῃ, καὶ οὐ θέλει μετανοῆσαι ἐκ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: And I gave to her time so that she might repent, and not she wills to repent of the immorality of her.
pieces: I gave her time to repent, and she is not willing to turn away from her sexual immorality.

L.21: And I gave her time so that she might repent, and she does not want to repent of her sexual immorality.

R.21: I have given her time to stop sinning and change her ways. But she does not want to give up her sexual sins.

decisions.choice: time to repent: judgment delayed for mercy's sake
decisions.reason: The delay of judgment gives room to repent (compare Romans 2:4; 2 Peter 3:9). The past "I gave" and the present "she does not want" set what Christ has done against what she still refuses.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality, and perhaps unfaithfulness to God
decisions.reason: See the note on 2:14.

records.source: ἰδοὺ βάλλω αὐτὴν εἰς κλίνην, καὶ τοὺς μοιχεύοντας μετ’ αὐτῆς εἰς θλῖψιν μεγάλην, ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσωσιν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῆς·
records.gloss: Behold I throw her into a bed, and those committing adultery with her into affliction great, if not they repent of the works of her;
pieces: Look, I am laying her on a sickbed, and those who commit adultery with her I am throwing into great affliction, unless they repent of the things she does.

L.22: Look, I am throwing her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her into great affliction, unless they repent of her works.

R.22: So I will make her sick, and she will have to stay in bed. And I will bring terrible suffering on the people who commit adultery with her, unless they stop doing what she does.

decisions.choice: a bed: a bed of sickness, in place of the bed of her immorality
alternatives: a dining couch at a feast
decisions.reason: κλίνην means a bed or couch. The bed of her sin becomes a bed of suffering, which suggests illness. The same word was used of the couches people lay on at banquets, which would fit the feasts with food sacrificed to idols, but the contrast with "great affliction" points to sickness.

decisions.choice: adultery: sharing in her sins, sexual and perhaps spiritual
decisions.reason: "Those who commit adultery with her" may be literal partners in sexual sin, or those who share in her unfaithfulness to God, as the prophets called idolatry adultery (Jeremiah 3:8-9; Ezekiel 23:37). The condition "unless they repent of her works" suggests a wider group than her lovers: those who follow her teaching.

decisions.choice: I am throwing: a present tense that announces a sure future
decisions.reason: βάλλω is present, but describes what is about to happen.

decisions.choice: a sickbed (B); make her sick ... stay in bed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense of illness that the word-sense decision takes as most likely.

records.source: καὶ τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς ἀποκτενῶ ἐν θανάτῳ· καὶ γνώσονται πᾶσαι αἱ ἐκκλησίαι ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἐραυνῶν νεφροὺς καὶ καρδίας, καὶ δώσω ὑμῖν ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: and the children of her I will kill with death; and will know all the churches that I am the [one] searching kidneys and hearts, and I will give to you each according to the works of you.
pieces: Her children I will put to death, and all the churches will come to know that I search the inner self, mind and heart, and that I will give each of you what your works deserve.

L.23: And I will kill her children with death, and all the churches will know that I am the one who searches kidneys and hearts, and I will give to each of you according to your works.

R.23: I will kill her children, those who follow her ways. Then all the churches will know that I see into people's deepest thoughts and feelings. I will pay each of you back for what you have done.

decisions.choice: her children: her followers
decisions.reason: Her "children" are most likely those who have taken her teaching as their own, as one may be a child of a teacher (compare 2 John 1, 4). Those who "commit adultery with her" (2:22) share in the sin; her children follow it.

decisions.choice: kill with death: put to death, perhaps by disease
decisions.reason: The phrase is emphatic. In 6:8 the same word for death means a deadly plague, and the Greek Old Testament often uses it that way, so disease may be meant here, matching the sickbed of 2:22.

decisions.choice: the one who searches minds and hearts: God's title in Jeremiah and the Psalms
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 17:10 says, "I the LORD search the heart and test the mind, to give to each according to his ways." Psalm 7:10 says the same of God. Christ takes this title for himself. νεφροὺς, literally "kidneys", stood for the seat of a person's desires and feelings; "hearts" for the mind and will. Together they mean the whole inner person.

decisions.choice: judgment by works
decisions.reason: Each one receives according to what they have done (compare Psalm 62:13; Romans 2:6; Revelation 20:12; 22:12). The judgment is personal: "each of you".

decisions.choice: kidneys and hearts (L); the inner self, mind and heart (B); deepest thoughts and feelings (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew way of speaking, which the Greek follows. Balanced and Readable say what it means in English (m3).

decisions.choice: those who follow her ways (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "her children" with the reading the word-sense decision takes as most likely.

records.source: ὑμῖν δὲ λέγω τοῖς λοιποῖς τοῖς ἐν Θυατείροις, ὅσοι οὐκ ἔχουσιν τὴν διδαχὴν ταύτην, οἵτινες οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τὰ βαθέα τοῦ Σατανᾶ, ὡς λέγουσιν, οὐ βάλλω ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἄλλο βάρος·
records.gloss: But to you I say, the rest the in Thyatira, as many as not have the teaching this, who not knew the deep things of the Satan, as they say, not I throw on you other burden;
pieces: But to the rest of you in Thyatira, all who do not hold this teaching and have not learned the deep things of Satan, as they call them, I say this: I will lay no other burden on you.

L.24: But to you I say, the rest in Thyatira, as many as do not have this teaching, who have not known the deep things of Satan, as they say: I am not putting on you another burden.

R.24: But some of you in Thyatira do not follow her teaching. You have not learned "the deep secrets of Satan," as they call them. I say to you: I will not give you any other load to carry.

decisions.choice: the deep things of Satan, as they say: a claim to secret knowledge
alternatives: they claimed to know "the deep things of God", and Christ calls them Satan's
they themselves said they had to learn Satan's depths in order to master them
decisions.reason: Jezebel's followers seem to have claimed a deeper knowledge than ordinary believers had. "As they say" may mean that they used the phrase "the deep things" (Paul speaks of "the depths of God", 1 Corinthians 2:10) and that Christ supplies "of Satan". Or they may have said that they could know Satan's depths, sharing in pagan feasts and immorality, without harm. The text allows both.

decisions.choice: no other burden: an echo of the decision of the Jerusalem council
decisions.reason: In Acts 15:28-29 the apostles wrote to the churches that they would lay on them no greater burden than to keep away from food sacrificed to idols and from sexual immorality, the very things Jezebel taught. The faithful in Thyatira are asked for nothing more than that, and to hold fast (2:25).

decisions.choice: the people addressed come first (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "to you I say" first and names the people after it. Balanced names them first, so the reader knows who is meant before the message; Readable makes them the subject of their own sentence.

records.source: πλὴν ὃ ἔχετε κρατήσατε ἄχρι οὗ ἂν ἥξω.
records.gloss: Only what you have hold fast until which [time] I come.
pieces: Just keep a firm grip on what you have until I come.

L.25: Only, what you have, hold fast until I come.

R.25: Just hold on tightly to what you have until I come.

decisions.choice: until I come: the final coming
decisions.reason: Here the coming has no condition attached, as it did in 2:5 and 2:16, and the faithful are to hold on until it: it is most likely the final coming of Christ.

records.source: καὶ ὁ νικῶν καὶ ὁ τηρῶν ἄχρι τέλους τὰ ἔργα μου, δώσω αὐτῷ ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν, καὶ ποιμανεῖ αὐτοὺς ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ ὡς τὰ σκεύη τὰ κεραμικὰ συντρίβεται, ὡς κἀγὼ εἴληφα παρὰ τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ δώσω αὐτῷ τὸν ἀστέρα τὸν πρωϊνόν.
records.gloss: And the [one] overcoming and the [one] keeping until end the works of me, I will give to him authority over the nations, \v 27 and he will shepherd them with a rod iron, as the vessels the clay are broken, \v 28 as I also have received from the Father of me, and I will give to him the star the morning.
pieces: To everyone who overcomes and keeps doing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} works to the end I will give authority over the nations.
{{gender:They|He}} will shepherd the nations with a rod of iron, as clay pots are smashed to pieces,
with the same authority I myself received from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father. And to each of them I will give the morning star.

L.26: And the one who overcomes and who keeps {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} works until [the] end, I will give {{gender:that person|him}} authority over the nations,
L.27: and {{gender:that person|he}} will shepherd them with an iron rod, as clay pots are shattered,
L.28: as I also have received from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father; and I will give {{gender:that person|him}} the morning star.

R.26: I will give power over the nations to everyone who wins the victory and keeps doing what I want until the end.
R.27: They will rule the nations with an iron rod and smash them to pieces like clay pots.
R.28: It is the same power that I received from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father. I will also give them the morning star.

decisions.choice: Psalm 2:8-9: authority over the nations
decisions.reason: In Psalm 2:8-9 God promises his king the nations as his inheritance, and says that he will break them with a rod of iron and shatter them like a potter's vessel. Revelation applies the psalm to Christ (12:5; 19:15) and here promises a share in his rule to those who overcome (compare 3:21; 20:4).

decisions.choice: shepherd: rule, here with a rod that breaks
decisions.reason: ποιμανεῖ means to tend a flock, and kings were called shepherds. The Greek Old Testament of Psalm 2:9 uses this verb where the Hebrew has "break". With a rod of iron and clay pots shattered, the rule is one of judgment on those who resist.

decisions.choice: the one who overcomes ... I will give him: the sentence starts again
decisions.reason: The Greek names the person first and then starts the sentence again with "I will give him".

decisions.choice: keeps my works: does the works I require, in contrast to her works
decisions.reason: "My works" stands against "her works" in 2:22: the faithful keep doing what Christ commands, not what Jezebel teaches.

decisions.choice: the morning star: Christ himself, and a share in his rule
alternatives: Venus, the planet that announces the dawn, as a sign of victory and rule
a share in the glory of the righteous, who shine like stars (Daniel 12:3)
decisions.reason: In 22:16 Jesus says, "I am the bright morning star." So the gift may be Christ himself. The morning star, the planet Venus, was also a sign of victory and royal power, which fits the promise of rule, and Numbers 24:17 speaks of a star that will come out of Jacob. These meanings can go together.

decisions.choice: as I also have received: authority given by the Father
decisions.reason: What Christ promises is the authority he himself received from his Father, as Psalm 2 says the Father gives it to his Son. The verb has no object; "authority" from verse 26 is understood.

decisions.choice: the nations (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the nations again so that "them" is not taken for the believers.

records.source: ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.
records.gloss: The [one] having an ear let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
pieces: Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches."

L.29: The one who has an ear, let {{gender:that person|him}} hear what the Spirit says to the churches."

R.29: Everyone who can hear should listen carefully to what the Spirit is saying to the churches."

decisions.choice: the call that closes every letter
decisions.reason: The same call ends each of the seven letters; see the notes on 2:7. What the risen Jesus says to one church, the Spirit says to all of them.
